The biggest constraint on your business growth isn't your product or market - it's your content operation. You're trying to scale a one-person show in a world that rewards systems.

We've analyzed over 200 founder brands. The pattern is clear: founders who DIY their content plateau fast. They hit 200-300 followers and stay there. Engagement stays below 50 likes. Inbound leads are non-existent. We see founders with 10K followers getting only 20 likes because the audience doesn't care about random posts. It's organized noise without strategy. Not because the content is bad, but because there's no engine behind it.

Your time is finite. Spending 10-15 hours a week on content means less time on sales, strategy, or leadership. The math breaks down. You're trading your highest-value hours for mediocre distribution.

We designed a different model. For a consultant in professional services, we built a full system: ICP research, competitor hook mapping, content batching, and automated posting. He approved posts in 20 minutes a week. We handled everything else.

Results in 90 days: from 80 followers to 12,000. From 5 likes per post to 2,500. Profile visits jumped from 10 to 450 per day. He closed three inbound deals worth five figures each.

This is how you scale without burning out. You invest in a system that compounds, not in hours spent writing. The agency becomes your growth engine - silent, systematic, and relentless.

Roadmaps are easy to read as reality, and the first time I opened the AINFT whitepaper, I mixed up what was already built with what was still a plan.

That is an easy mistake, so I went back and read Whitepaper V2.0 from September 2025 slowly, with one question in mind: what is on paper, and what can I actually see today?

Here is the paper version, four business lines:
➜ AINFT Agent Framework, a multi-agent system with Core API message passing, event-driven scheduling, plus AgentChat, Extensions and Magentic APIs
➜ AINFT Nova, a no-code agent launch platform where each agent can issue its own token, "one agent, one economy"
➜ AINFT AgenTX, a FinAgent framework for medium-to-low frequency multi-chain DeFi with ML forecasting, reinforcement learning and DAO-governed parameters
➜ AINFT Grid, decentralized model training on distributed compute with smart-contract task scheduling and incentives

Underneath sit the roadmap layers:
➜ An AI Agent Layer with DID registration
➜ An SDK Layer and a User Interaction Layer
➜ An Incentive Layer and the Agent Commerce Protocol

That is an ambitious stack, and I like that it is specific rather than vague.

Now the honest part.

An independent Protos review in February 2026 said Nova, Agent Framework, AgenTX and Grid had not launched at that time.

What I can see on the AINFT site today is narrower: the AI Trading Agent Benchmark, and even that is labelled coming soon, private preview.

So my gap analysis looks like this:
➜ Designed: 𝗳𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗱𝘂𝗰𝘁 𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗲𝘀 with real technical detail
➜ Visible: one evaluation product, on BTC and ETH paper markets only
➜ Missing: public launch dates for Nova, Agent Framework, AgenTX and Grid

I do want to give credit where it is due.

The benchmark is not random; it maps neatly onto AgenTX, because you cannot responsibly run a trading agent before you can measure one.

The TRON H1 2026 Strategy Report also places AINFT in the trading-strategy validation layer, which tells me the focus has narrowed on purpose.

𝗡𝗮𝗿𝗿𝗼𝘄𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗶𝘀 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗳𝗮𝗶𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗴.

Plenty of whitepapers try to ship everything at once and ship nothing well.

My open question is sequencing: does Nova come before AgenTX, and will Grid wait until there is real demand for decentralized training?

If the team publishes dates and milestones for each line, this whitepaper becomes a checklist we can all track together.

Read it yourself and tell me which line you think should ship next:

X 已将复制链接分享的排名权重从 20 降至 0。

这此前是已公布模型中权重最高的正面信号之一。

以下是 10 月 27 日至 11 月 15 日期间的其他变化：

• 点赞：+7.3%
• 一般分享：+5.9%
• 连续阅读时间：+25%
• 帖子点击：-8.7%
• 点击相关阅读时间：-3.8%
• 视频打开：降至零
• 复制链接分享：降至零
• “不感兴趣”：负面权重略微增强

几点值得了解的事项。

1. 阅读时间正变得越来越重要。

X 已在 10 月更新了其检索系统，以更好地识别用户完整阅读的帖子。

现在，连续停留时间系数又增加了 25%。

对于创作者来说，这为有实质内容的帖子提供了有力理由。一个强有力的开篇能吸引注意力，但其余部分需要值得一读。

2. X 正在改变其使用你浏览历史的方式。

最新的代码使排名服务能够接收多达 50 个先前提供的帖子的信息。

这为系统提供了更多关于某人已看过内容的上下文，并可能帮助其避免重复推荐。

对于创作者来说，反复发布相同的回收观点可能会变得不太有效。

3. 分享仍然重要，但并非所有分享都平等。

复制链接信号降至零尤为引人注目。

与此同时，一般分享的权重有所增加，而回复、引用和 DM 分享仍保持重要的正面信号。

一个重要的区别：这些权重应用于预测行为，而非原始互动计数。一个回复并不自动等同于五个点赞。

4. 算法越来越专注于预测有意义的互动。

我对这些变化的解读是，X 更加强调人们是否真正想花时间阅读帖子、讨论它并分享它。

不再有理由只痴迷于点击量。

一个注意事项：这些是公共代码默认值。X 可以运行不同设置的实验，因此我们不能假设每个用户看到的排名行为完全相同。

如果你想深入研究，完整源代码是公开的：


https://
github.com/xai-org/x-algo
rithm
…

OK before anyone gets too serious on this one...
This is a real account of my personal trip and I was WAAAAY to tired to do this safely and would not advise anyone else repeating this.
I myself never want to do it again and agree that it is stupid.
I probably almost fell asleep 7 times and this trip would not be possible without FSD.
*******************************
(DO NOT DO THIS)
*******************************
It was dumb of me to do it and I will not be doing it ever again if I can help it.   I recently picked up my New 2026 Model Y from Tesla and honestly, it’s a pretty awesome car. Here's the pro’s con’s and other info.
I Left Dryden at Midnight November 10th
My father drove me to Winnipeg a ~4h drive for a 2.5 h flight to Toronto.
I arrived in Toronto, then took a 15 minute cab ride down to Etobicoke for the pickup. (Yes I asked multiple times and they won't deliver closer... FML...🤦)  My appointment was scheduled for the 11th month on the 11thday at the 11th hour.
11,11,11 :D
I arrived around 9 and the Tesla Center wasn’t open until 10. The cab driver had dropped me off at the front door inside the fenced area. This was amusing because everything was closed and the only exit was where he drover in.
Basically I was early so I awkwardly walked around and looked at some cars before realizing I probably wasn’t supposed to be in there yet.
I left to go get a drink and went back at about 10. They let me go in and start my paperwork right way. The staff at the Tesla Center were pretty good. He showed me the car, ran through the features, tested out FSD and talked about a few other issues or concerns I had.
I asked about accessories and was a little disappointed in the lack of stuff available on site. I did pick up a charging cord for my home, but there wasn’t much else there for accessories at all.
I was honestly hoping for a show room or at least an air mattress or something. Anyways... There was an Optimus at least 😅
By about ~11:30 I was off for my very very very long drive home... I let FSD take over almost the entire drive home and it actually did surprisingly well. It navigated amazingly, parked itself most of the time, and had very little issues in total.
"This car is amazing at city driving"
It's basically like taking a cab, country driving needs some work still. 🤷
Here are the few issues it did have. Please note that these issues occurred over the span of 1700+ km and were not present the whole time. I was waaaaay to tired to be driving and was definitely way more of a safety risk than FSD could ever be.
These issues were only present for short periods during the entire 1700+ km drive.   1) Speed limit signs. The FSD system seemed to have a problem with not seeing or completely disregarding speed limit signs in certain areas. This happened mostly outside of the area before Blind River, and then again much closer to home.
For a vision based system, I am unsure how it could miss 3x speed change signs multiple times? There is usually a Speed sign with an arrow signifying the speed limit will change up ahead, another sign without an arrow signifying this is where the speed changes, followed by a third sign just in case you missed the first 2... Yet the Tesla would stay going 90 when it dropped to 60 or 70kpm or insist it was still 60 or 70kph when it went back up to 90. This should probably be fixed...
There is also the yellow signs with sharp angles and advisable speeds for sharp corners and stuff, yea.. FSD should probably pay attention to those too...
Nothing wakes you up like a 90 degree right arrow that says like 30kph and the cars like fuck that, lets do 90 🤣
(I Suggest adding a cruise toggle or control feature where you can manually set the desired speed and FSD will try and maintain it)
Maybe just have it on the screen or use one of the toggle wheels on the steering wheel so you can adjust it like many adaptable cruise control systems. This would allow people to adjust it to the proper speed without having to jerk it out of FSD and the car could learn from the consistency across the network.
2) Freezing Rain and Icy road conditions. Yes I know people are probably going to say, “you shouldn’t use FSD in those conditions” “this is an unfair test” so forth whine whine.
The bottom line is this. FSD will eventually drive everyone everywhere in all road conditions, there's no point in babying it if you want it to learn. FSD actually did really good, there were only two major issues and one of them may have been related to ice buildup in the frontal camera combined with someone else's trailer or something.   Firstly, FSD NEEDS to be able to assess icy road conditions and adjust brakes accordingly. Sudden or rough braking on ice is just asking for problems.
The car still handled fine, but when approaching another vehicle going 20kph slower due to icy road conditions, maybe don’t use the brakes last second so that you skid up behind them? it’s not city driving so the car should adjust accordingly. Slow deceleration, slow into the corners and faster out, no sudden speed changes, you know, icy road driving...
The second was a rare instance of what can only be described as a "death wobble". Basically the car came up behind another vehicle with a tow load. The car then decided that going slightly left, then right, then slightly more left then right, then slightly more left then right, in a slowly increasing fashion on an icy road was a good idea? Yea... it is NOT...😐😅It is a good way to test the vehicles stability in a small recovery skid though... FYI it’s incredibly stable due to it’s low center of gravity and could probably drift a 90 degree corner at 100km an hour if you wanted to try it.
(not recommended though 😅)
I actually needed to disengage FSD on this one because it would have gotten dangerous fast... This could have been due to the frontal camera being iced up a bit, or the car trying to recover from a slide/skid coming in behind the other vehicle. Regardless, it needs to be looked at for sure.     3) parking panic and then just not caring. FSD kinda panicked when trying to park for charging when all the lines were covered up, it’s ok but a little amusing that a light dusting of snow cripples the parking feature. Slightly later it didn’t seem to care about the lines or lining up at all, I actually had to adjust the parking manually just so the charge cord would reach, I found this a little odd. Maybe it was related to loss of signal or something, I know cell reception out this way is often non existent for massive areas. I find this behavior odd as it usually parks itself perfectly, I was actually really impressed by the smoothness of it when I picked it up. Suggestion. Maybe have it line up with the charging stations themselves? It can stull use all the obstacle avoidance features of the driving, but have it line up with the charge station when the lines aren't available. This would allow people to still line up for charging even if the lines are a problem.   Overall FSD gets 4.9 Stars out of 5. The car passes, navigates, drives, avoids obstacles (dodged a tire on the road) parks, and does everything its supposed to do. I am still testing it and considering looking for some studded winter tire options. Overall it’s really really damn good. I arrived home just before 10:30 am November 12th, this means I was physically up and awake for ~35 hours. 23 of these hours were in the drivers seat with only short charging naps, usually ~15 minutes or so, this thing charges FAST!
Again I “DO NOT” recommend doing this... (I probably almost fell asleep 7 times 😑)  DON’T DO THIS!!!
I DO recommend having that air mattress option in stock and really pushing sales for anyone who plans on driving more than 5 hours on pickup...
If anyone has any questions, feel free to ask, I’m more than happy to go find out some new stuff too if I don’t yet know.

When evaluating a stablecoin, its price peg is only one part of the conversation.

The governance model, transparency, security architecture and practical utility are equally important.

This is where USDD (
@USDDio
) deserves a closer look.

Built around decentralization and user empowerment, USDD brings together several features designed to support a more accessible and transparent stablecoin ecosystem.

Here are six important things to understand:

🔹 Decentralized Governance: USDD incorporates community-driven governance through proposals and on-chain voting, giving governance participants a role in shaping the ecosystem.

🔹 Transparency & Auditability: Blockchain records make transactions and relevant collateral information publicly verifiable, allowing users to examine important aspects of the system.

🔹 Over-Collateralization: USDD uses an over-collateralized reserve framework designed to provide additional backing and help manage market fluctuations. This does not eliminate market or protocol risks, but it is an important part of its stability architecture.

🔹 DeFi Integration: USDD can participate in decentralized financial activities such as lending, borrowing, savings and trading across supported applications.

🔹 Freeze-Free Transactions: USDD held in a self-custodial on-chain wallet cannot be directly frozen at the token level by a centralized authority. Users still need to consider smart contract, wallet and network risks.

🔹 Multichain Accessibility: USDD currently supports TRON, Ethereum and BNB Chain through its application, expanding its reach across different blockchain environments.

But here's the bigger picture.

A useful stablecoin should offer more than a dollar-denominated value. It should provide accessible infrastructure, transparent mechanisms and practical opportunities within the digital economy.

USDD brings these elements together in its approach to decentralized finance.

Understanding these fundamentals is an important step toward understanding where decentralized stablecoins fit into the future of finance.

⚖️ NIGERIA POLITICS DEBATE: Bola Tinubu (Lagos) vs. Peter Obi (Anambra) — Who Left the Stronger Record as Governor?

As campaigns heat up ahead of the January 2027 presidential election, one of the biggest debates dividing Nigerians online and at campaign rallies is the comparison between Bola Tinubu’s two terms as Governor of Lagos State (1999–2007) and Peter Obi’s two terms as Governor of Anambra State (2006–2014).

According to political analysts, party spokespersons, and public governance debates across Nigeria, both camps point to very different leadership styles and achievements:

 * The Case for Bola Tinubu in Lagos (1999–2007):

   Supporters and APC spokespersons point to Tinubu’s financial engineering and long-term master plan for Lagos. When former President Olusegun Obasanjo withheld Lagos local government funds, Tinubu’s administration overhauled the state's tax system—boosting Internally Generated Revenue (IGR, meaning money the state raises locally without waiting for Abuja) from a few hundred million naira monthly to billions. His backers also credit him with laying the institutional blueprint for Lagos’s modern transportation (BRT), waste management, and power projects, while mentoring a team of successors who carried those plans forward.

   • What critics say: Opponents argue that Lagos already enjoyed a massive head start as Nigeria's former federal capital and commercial hub, and question the high cost of governance and debt profile left behind.

 * The Case for Peter Obi in Anambra (2006–2014):
   Supporters and public development commentators point to Obi’s strict cost-cutting, prudence, and focus on human capital despite Anambra’s much smaller revenue base. Backers highlight his partnership with the church to hand back and revitalize mission schools—which pushed Anambra to the top of national WAEC and NECO rankings—alongside expanding rural road networks and leaving billions of naira in cash and investments in state reserves without borrowing from banks.

   • What critics say: Presidency spokespersons and critics argue that saving money in banks rather than spending aggressively on mega-infrastructure held back faster industrial growth, and question his succession planning and local government elections during his tenure.

One question every stablecoin user should ask is simple:

Can I independently examine the system responsible for protecting the value of the asset I hold?

This question matters because a stablecoin's credibility should not depend entirely on what its developers say about it. Its underlying mechanisms should also be open to inspection.

This is an important part of the infrastructure behind USDD (
@USDDio
).

Let's look at three areas where transparency becomes practical rather than just a marketing promise.

🔹 1. Visible Collateral Infrastructure

USDD uses a collateral-backed model. Its official documentation provides contract addresses that users can examine through supported blockchain explorers.

This gives participants a way to inspect relevant on-chain balances and understand where protocol collateral is held.

🔹 2. Transparent Protocol Operations

Through its Vault system, users can examine collateral positions, outstanding debt and collateralization ratios.

These details matter because maintaining a healthy collateral position is essential to managing liquidation risks and supporting the protocol's financial structure.

🔹 3. Accessible Peg Stability Mechanism

USDD's Peg Stability Module (PSM) provides a conversion mechanism between USDD and supported stablecoins at a fixed 1:1 rate.

Rather than relying entirely on conventional decentralized exchange price curves, the PSM provides another route for stablecoin conversion and supports the protocol's peg-management approach.

Transparency is not simply about publishing information.

It is about giving users the tools to investigate, understand and evaluate the infrastructure behind their assets.

Of course, on-chain visibility does not eliminate smart contract vulnerabilities, market volatility or collateral risks. Users still need to conduct independent research.

But when important protocol information can be examined rather than accepted blindly, users have a stronger foundation for making informed decisions.

That's an important principle for the future of decentralized finance: don't just ask users to trust the system. Give them the ability to verify it.

As more observers apply the Three-Track Model to contemporary relationship dynamics, a natural question arises: once we recognize that removing post-agricultural Institutional Scaffolding has exposed the raw Biological Floor, what is the prescriptive solution for the future?

First, a strict methodological boundary must be stated. The purpose of this work is not to serve as a normative guide to the future or to prescribe a political or cultural reconstruction. In empirical science, diagnostic cartography must remain separate from ideological prescription. My sole objective is to map the present landscape with maximum accuracy so that observers can read the environment as it actually functions.

Second, the confusion surrounding modern mating chaos disappears the moment we recognize that the Three-Track architecture governs all domains of human cooperation, not just reproduction.

1. The Universal Architecture of Social Technology

In Dual-Inheritance Theory (gene-culture coevolution), researchers such as Peter Richerson and Robert Boyd (2005) and Ara Norenzayan et al. (2016) have demonstrated that large-scale post-agricultural civilizations could not function solely on raw Pleistocene instincts. Across every domain of survival, human behavior is sorted across three distinct bins:

The Biological Floor: Conserved, self-interested evolutionary algorithms selected to maximize individual inclusive fitness and survival under ancestral conditions.

Institutional Scaffolding: Co-evolved legal, religious, economic, and reputational technologies that impose external costs on floor defection, making large-scale cooperation and long-term contracts stable.

The Cultural Canopy: The idealized moral or romantic narrative that a society layers over its institutions to describe human cooperation in flattering terms.

2. The Criminology Analogy: Why Only Mating Surprises Us

Evolutionary psychologists Martin Daly and Margo Wilson (1988) and David Buss and Todd Shackelford (1997) have extensively documented that the human Biological Floor contains conditional, context-dependent modules for resource expropriation (theft, raiding) and interpersonal aggression. When the expected payoff of seizing another person's resources exceeds the expected cost of punishment, the floor strategy activates.

In the domains of property and violent crime, society does not confuse the Cultural Canopy with the Institutional Scaffolding. No rational policymaker assumes that human civic politeness is self-sustaining, and no one proposes abolishing locks, police enforcement, property titles, and criminal penalties on the assumption that "mutual respect" will prevent burglary. If a city dismantled its legal scaffolding on Monday and experienced widespread looting on Tuesday, no observer would diagnose the population with a mysterious new psychological disorder. They would recognize that removing external constraints exposes baseline opportunistic behavior.

3. The Mating Exception and the Collapse of the Rails

In the domain of human reproduction and pair-bonding, however, contemporary culture committed that exact error.

Post-agricultural monogamous marriage was a high-constraint social technology built to align male provisioning, female hypergamy, and paternity certainty by pricing out opportunistic floor behavior (Henrich, Boyd, & Richerson, 2012; Fortunato & Archetti, 2010). Over time, our culture mistook the decorative Romantic Canopy (the story that soulmate emotion holds families together) for the load-bearing structure.

Operating under that illusion, society systematically removed the legal, economic, and reputational scaffolding around pair-bonding while leaving the biological hardware unchanged. Today, we watch unfiltered Strategic Pluralism (Gangestad & Simpson, 2000), partner-specific erotic habituation (Klusmann, 2002), the Coolidge effect (Symons, 1979), modular partition defense (Kurzban & Aktipis, 2007), and rational male market withdrawal (Baumeister & Vohs, 2004) execute in the open.

There is no mystery in the contemporary relationship landscape: while historical scaffolding was often harsh and punitive, demolishing an archaic constraint system without installing a viable replacement does not eliminate human conflict; it simply strips away the institutional regulation of an ancient biological drive and defaults the market back to the raw evolutionary floor.

👉 S1 Watch #11: Google just joined the S1 race. Your release gate shouldn't change.💥

🙋 What's new
Google DeepMind released Gemini Decision 1 and a Gemini Decisions API. 

Like Jev, it writes no prose. It returns typed answers with confidence scores your code can act on, and it reads text, images, audio, video and PDFs together, up to 1,000 questions about the same material in one pass (VentureBeat).

Google joins the list this S1 Watch series tracks: 
 ⇒ Jev, 
 ⇒ Microsoft-Decision-1, 
 ⇒ OpenAI's Decisions API, 
 ⇒ Perplexity, 
 ⇒ Liquid AI, 
 ⇒ Drex, 
and now Gemini.

🤔 What's exciting
1️⃣ Multimodal checklists. A claim with a form, photos and a call recording can be screened in one request.
2️⃣ Independent referees are arriving. Artificial Analysis's Decision Index v2 rewards calibration, not just accuracy.
3️⃣ The interface is standardizing. As Pete Johnson put it in CIO, the interface standardized before the market did. That's what makes S1s swappable.

 Where I'm skeptical
🔸Self-run benchmarks. In Google's own launch tests, Gemini led five of seven. On Artificial Analysis's independent index, it launched ninth of 18. Same model, different referee.
🔸Right answers aren't a right case. That index's document test only counts a document when every answer on it is correct. The whole case is what you release.
🔸A probability is not a decision. Even TypeSafe says it plainly: "Jev makes judgments, code makes decisions."
🔸 Inputs can be steered. VentureBeat reports a single planted field dropped Jev's probability of blocking an action from 0.76 to 0.48. A model that can be talked down should never be what releases an answer.

🛠️ How we handle that in ModelFusion
▫️ Jev runs in production in our document lane, where it can discard a bad contributor draft. It filters. It doesn't release.
▫️ Only the deterministic audit gate can release an answer.
▫️ Every run leaves unsigned inspection receipts: what was checked, and why it passed or failed.
▫️ Gemini joins the rest on our watch list, not integrated.

Google's entry confirms there won't be a single winner.

What's your S1 bet: pick one lab and hope, or keep the gate yours and swap the scorer?

In October 2008 Henry Waxman said the CEOs of S&P, Moody's and Fitch, paid over $80 million between them, would testify that virtually no one saw it coming. Then he read Moody's and S&P files. An S&P analyst had written: "it could be structured by cows, and we would rate it."

The bill came years later. S&P paid $1.375 billion in 2015 and Moody's $864 million in 2017 to settle with the Justice Department and the states. The hearing that laid out the case costs nothing.

In the video below, Waxman reads the documents into the record in a 13-minute opening statement. Listen to what the CEO of Moody's told his own board a year earlier.

The House recording has been on the Internet Archive since February 2011. It has 118 downloads.

Waxman had done this before. In April 1994 he chaired the hearing where seven tobacco CEOs each said under oath that they did not believe nicotine was addictive. In 2008 he gave his verdict on a new industry:

"The story of the credit rating agencies is a story of a colossal failure."

Taken together, the documents leave four rules.

Ask who pays the grader. The banks selling the bonds paid for the ratings. Revenue at the three firms doubled, from about $3 billion in 2002 to over $6 billion in 2007.

Quality has no customer. In October 2007 Moody's CEO Raymond McDaniel told his board that issuers wanted high ratings and investors did not want downgrades. In his words, "ratings quality has surprisingly few friends."

Volume drowns out warnings. A month earlier, at an internal town hall, McDaniel said rivals rated everything investment grade in 2004 and 2005, and Moody's warnings went nowhere: "No one cared, because the machine just kept going."

Check what the model leaves out. In the full chat, read later in the hearing by Rep. John Yarmuth, the same analyst said the model did not capture half the risk. The SEC had printed the same chat in July 2008 without naming the firm.

Those were the CEOs who, Waxman said, would claim virtually no one saw it coming. S&P's settlement alone was about 17 times the $80 million the three had made.

Waxman ended his opening with a warning:

"The result is that our entire financial system is now at risk, just as the CEO of Moody's predicted a year ago."

The full hearing is free on the Internet Archive, posted from the House recording in 2011. It sits under a dry committee title, Part 1 of 2, where few people look.

Were the rating agencies wrong to sell grades to the banks that paid for them, or were investors wrong to hand their judgment to a firm the seller paid?

You can read about system design for weeks. The real round is still a conversation.

Someone asks why you picked Redis. Someone asks what breaks at 10x traffic. And you have 45 minutes.

SysRound is a voice AI interviewer for system design practice. You talk to Alex the same way you talk to a human interviewer.

How a round works:
1. Pick one of 267 questions. Candidates reported them from real onsite interviews.
2. Talk by voice or by text. Draw on a shared whiteboard with notes.
3. Alex, the AI interviewer, answers requirement questions like a product owner.
4. Alex reads the whiteboard while you draw and asks about the hard parts.
5. Alex watches the time and tells you when to move to the next step.

A round is 45 or 60 minutes. It has the steps of an onsite round. First come requirements and estimation. Then the API, the data model and a high level design. Then detailed questions on the hard parts, and a summary.

What you get at the end:
- A score for each of seven skills, compared with the level you target
- Quotes of what you said or drew, next to each score
- A model answer that starts from your own notes
- A minute by minute replay of the whiteboard
- A practice plan for your weakest skills

During the beta, you get 2 free rounds of 45 minutes. After that, rounds come in packs. There is no subscription.

The AI interviewer and the feedback can be wrong. Use it for practice, not for hiring.
